title: DashGuard: spatio-temporal deep learning for dashcam-based road accident anticipation
task: Spatio-temporal deep learning for dashcam-based road accident anticipation
key_results: Two-Stream Transformer achieved AUC = 0.981 and F1 = 0.870 on Car Crash Dataset; lightweight 3D CNN (180K params) achieves AUC = 0.949 for edge deployment
comments: Rigorous evaluation with leak-free protocol and temporal consistency gating; two-stream attention shows clear advantage over single-stream designs.

model_io.model: Six spatio-temporal models: 3D CNN, CNN+LSTM, CNN+Transformer, two-stream lightweight CNN, two-stream ResNet-18, two-stream Transformer
inputs: dashcam video clips (1500 crash + 2000 normal videos)
outputs: soft temporal labels (distance to accident frame)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Two-stream architecture explicitly separating motion and appearance outperforms single-stream designs for accident anticipation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Two-Stream Transformer achieved best performance (AUC = 0.981, F1 = 0.870) with high recall (0.991)

title: An integrated bidirectional LSTM and adaptive cubature Kalman filter estimation method for accurate state-of-charge estimation of lithium-ion battery
task: State-of-charge estimation for lithium-ion battery using BiLSTM-Adaptive Cubature Kalman Filter
key_results: BiLSTM-ACKF achieved 40-60% RMSE reduction vs standalone BiLSTM and 30-52% vs BiLSTM-AEKF across four drive cycles; maintained <1.5% error over all test cases
comments: Tight coupling of neural network and filtering with adaptive covariance and cubature propagation eliminates first-order linearization bias; robust across temperatures and noise levels.

model_io.model: Bidirectional LSTM (sequence encoder) → Adaptive Cubature Kalman Filter (single-RC Thevenin model)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tight coupling of BiLSTM output as SOC pseudo-measurement with adaptive cubature-based Kalman filtering outperforms loosely coupled approaches
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 40-60% RMSE reduction vs BiLSTM alone and 30-52% vs BiLSTM-AEKF with consistent upper bound <1.5% error

title: Deployment of edge-lightweight AI vertical models in multimodal anomaly detection and energy optimization of tech-long production line
task: Edge-lightweight AI for multimodal anomaly detection and energy optimization in packaging production line
key_results: FeatherCNN anomaly accuracy 0.931; model compression reduced FLOPs from 3.42×10⁹ to 0.58×10⁹ (83% reduction); inference latency 18.63→7.41 ms; dual-layer control reduced energy consumption by 26%
comments: Practical edge AI deployment combining multimodal fusion, aggressive quantization (INT4), and real-time energy control; significant FLOPs reduction without sacrificing anomaly detection accuracy.

model_io.model: Multimodal FeatherCNN (vibration+acoustic+thermal) → Dual-layer control chain
inputs: vibration, acoustic, thermal signals from bottle blowing/filling/packaging

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multimodal lightweight CNN with dual-layer collaborative control achieves high anomaly detection and energy optimization on resource-constrained ARM edge controllers
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 0.931 anomaly accuracy, 83% FLOPs reduction, 26% energy consumption reduction on packaging line

title: Evaluating the accuracy and efficiency of Cloud-to-IDA for drift-based collapse assessment of steel frames under near- and far-field motions
task: Cloud-to-IDA procedure for drift-based collapse fragility assessment of steel moment-resisting frames
key_results: Cloud-to-IDA reduced computational time by 86-91% vs IDA while limiting median collapse-capacity errors to a few percent; conventional Cloud Analysis showed height-dependent bias up to 20% on 3-story frames
comments: Cloud-to-IDA provides efficient alternative to IDA for fragility assessment with robust median/dispersion estimates; applicability carefully bounded to studied frame heights and collapse criteria.

model_io.model: Conventional Cloud Analysis vs Cloud-to-IDA procedure using OpenSees nonlinear simulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cloud-to-IDA provides accurate and computationally efficient collapse fragility estimates comparable to IDA with reduced bias
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Cloud-to-IDA errors <few%, 86-91% computational savings; conventional Cloud shows height-dependent bias up to 20%

title: Distribution-based canonical correlation residual monitoring for industrial processes fault detection
task: Fault detection in industrial processes using distribution-based CCA residual monitoring
key_results: CCA-KD (Kantorovich Distance) achieved best overall performance with high detection and low false-alarm rates on Williams-Otto reactor and WWTP; outperforms CCA-SPE, PCA, SVR methods
comments: Distribution-based monitoring avoids Gaussian assumptions and requires only fault-free data; effective across diverse fault types (bias, drift, freezing, intermittent).

model_io.model: CCA with Hellinger Distance (HD), Kullback-Leibler Distance (KLD), Kantorovich Distance (KD) + Kernel Density Estimation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Distribution-based CCA residual monitoring outperforms conventional CCA-SPE and competing methods for multivariate fault detection
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CCA-KD achieved best overall performance with high detection rates and low false-alarm rates across fault types

title: ZAPP: a zero-aware photovoltaic power prediction framework
task: Zero-aware photovoltaic power prediction with near-zero error reduction
key_results: sMAPE reduced from 60.57% to 11.07% on Dataset 1 and 63.30% to 11.92% on Dataset 2 using two-stage refinement (ZeroGate + low-power MAPE reducer)
comments: Two-stage approach effectively handles class imbalance and near-zero prediction errors without sacrificing overall regression metrics; simple but effective design.

model_io.model: Base regression (Persistence, Ridge, XGBoost, LSTM, Transformer, hybrid) → ZeroGate → Low-power MAPE reducer

hypotheses.hypothesis: Two-stage refinement with zero-prediction gating and low-power MAPE reduction outperforms unified regression for near-zero PV forecasting
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; sMAPE improved from ~60% to ~11% while maintaining R² > 0.95 on both datasets

title: Performance-based evaluation of hyperbolic and parabolic vertical curves for highway geometric design
task: Comparing dynamic performance of hyperbolic vs parabolic vertical curves in highway design
key_results: Hyperbolic curves produced vertical acceleration peaks of 0.590 m/s² vs 0.030 m/s² for parabolic; hyperbolic reduced wheel loads by 20-30% and suspension deflection by 15-20% under sag conditions
comments: Rigorous vehicle-dynamics comparison using CarSim simulation, though results suggest trade-offs rather than clear superiority of either approach.

model_io.model: CarSim vehicle dynamics simulator
inputs: stopping sight distance (SSD) and passing sight distance (PSD) criteria

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hyperbolic vertical curves exhibit different dynamic-performance characteristics than parabolic curves under standard highway-design constraints
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; substantial differences observed across all four performance indicators, with trade-offs favoring hyperbolic for wheel load but parabolic for vertical acceleration

title: SpecLLM: LLM-based VNIR spectral interpretation
task: LLM-based VNIR spectral interpretation using compact feature representations
key_results: Compact feature representations (natural language and JSON) substantially more effective than raw CSV/JSON/XML encodings; natural language reduces prompt length and provides human interpretability
comments: Interesting approach to serializing spectroscopy for LLMs, but performance still below Random Forest on raw spectra; trade-off between interpretability and raw accuracy.

model_io.model: LLM (unspecified) with natural-language or JSON feature encoding

hypotheses.hypothesis: Compact feature-based LLM representations outperform raw numerical encodings for spectral substance classification
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for LLM-based approaches; natural-language format more interpretable than raw spectra

title: Adaptive storage optimization for deep learning workloads in converged HPC-cloud environments: a reinforcement learning approach
task: Adaptive storage optimization for deep learning workloads using reinforcement learning
key_results: RL framework reduced checkpoint write latency by up to 74.6% and improved GPU utilization across ResNet-50, 3D U-Net, and Whisper Large workloads
comments: Temporally aware storage control shows promise, but evaluation limited to three workloads; generalization claims warrant further validation.

model_io.model: Proximal Policy Optimization + Soft Actor-Critic with Transformer state encoder
inputs: I/O traces from deep learning training phases

hypotheses.hypothesis: Temporally aware storage control can improve distributed training efficiency better than stateless parameter selection
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; RL-based policies achieved up to 74.6% latency reduction and consistent GPU utilization improvements

title: Transformer-based architectures for anomaly detection in solar-wind integrated energy infrastructures
task: Transformer-based anomaly detection in solar-wind integrated energy systems
key_results: Transformer achieved MSE = 0.00641 vs 0.00831 (LSTM), 0.00859 (GRU), 0.00792 (CNN-LSTM); accuracy 95% and ROC-AUC 0.89 but severe class imbalance (18.8:1) caused 0% recall on anomalies
comments: Model shows strong performance metrics on majority class but fails on minority (anomaly) class; severe class imbalance not adequately addressed, limiting practical utility.

model_io.model: Transformer encoder with multi-head self-attention vs LSTM, GRU, CNN-LSTM
inputs: multivariate time series from renewable energy facility: solar radiation, wind speed, temperature, humidity, power generation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Transformer with multi-head self-attention outperforms LSTM, GRU, CNN-LSTM for anomaly detection in renewable energy systems
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed on majority class; transformer MSE lowest (0.00641) but recall = 0% on true anomalies due to class imbalance

title: XCAT-UIR: explainable cross-attention guided ConvNeXt-transformer framework for underwater image restoration systems
task: Explainable cross-attention guided ConvNeXt-Transformer for underwater image restoration
key_results: XCAT-UIR improved underwater image quality through cross-attention fusion of ConvNeXt local and Swin Transformer global features; Grad-CAM and attention maps provide visual evidence of restoration decisions
comments: Hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture with explicit attention visualization addresses color attenuation and scattering; interpretability mechanism supports deployment in exploration/surveillance contexts.

model_io.model: ConvNeXt + Swin Transformer + Cross-Attention Fusion + Residual Reconstruction + Grad-CAM/attention-map visualization
inputs: underwater images degraded by light absorption/scattering

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cross-attention fusion of CNN texture and Transformer context features with explicit visualization outperforms single-architecture approaches for underwater image restoration
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; improved restoration performance with anatomically interpretable attention maps indicating model reasoning

title: A two-stage optimization method for wide-range single-electron quantum magnetic sensing
task: Protocol optimization for single-electron quantum magnetic sensing using two-stage learning
key_results: Two-stage method (Bayesian neural network + federated reinforcement learning) achieved significant improvements in accuracy and resource efficiency vs state-of-the-art on NV-center spin systems
comments: Novel hybrid approach combining model-based narrowing and RL calibration, but quantitative performance metrics not explicitly stated in abstract.

model_io.model: Bayesian Neural Network → Federated Reinforcement Learning Agent

hypotheses.hypothesis: Two-stage optimization with predictive phase narrowing outperforms black-box AI or formula-driven search for wide-range quantum sensing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; improved accuracy and resource efficiency on NV-center spin system with single-shot readout

title: Explainable machine learning for identifying nonlinear associations between street vitality and the built environment in a Historic District
task: Explainable machine learning for nonlinear street-vitality associations in historic district
key_results: XGBoost achieved R² = 0.474-0.490 under random validation but collapsed to R² = 0.012-0.084 under spatial GroupKFold; distance-to-heritage-core apparent importance inflated by spatial position
comments: Critical lesson on validation methodology: random validation masks spatial non-transferability and spurious correlations; SHAP attributions reflect spatial confounding rather than causal effects.

model_io.model: OLS, GAM, XGBoost with SHAP + LOWESS + spatial validation
inputs: heritage location, facilities, accessibility, street networks, frontage, streetscape visual features

hypotheses.hypothesis: XGBoost with SHAP reveals nonlinear within-area associations better than GAM/OLS, but random validation overstates spatial transferability
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; XGBoost outperforms on random split (R² = 0.474) but spatial GroupKFold reveals severe non-transferability (R² = 0.012-0.084)

title: Divergent financing responses in lithium exploration: descriptive time-series evidence from fiscal and enterprise channels (2015–2024)
task: Descriptive time-series analysis of lithium exploration financing across fiscal and enterprise channels
key_results: Higher lagged lithium prices associated with increased public expenditure and declining enterprise share; annual price increases linked to higher enterprise financing share
comments: Explicitly cautious interpretation: descriptive associations only, not causal; short time series (2015-2024) and institutional context limit generalizability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Public and enterprise financing channels respond differently to lithium price conditions
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed with descriptive patterns; lagged vs contemporaneous price effects differ by channel, but causal inference not supported

title: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS
task: Spatial isomer resolution on surfaces using Orbitrap secondary ion mass spectrometry
key_results: Successfully discriminated isomeric trisaccharides (raffinose, maltotriose, melezitose) and spatially resolved raffinose and maltotriose in mixtures; OrbiSIMS transmission behavior consistent with ion mobility spectrometry trends
comments: Structure-dependent dissociation and collisional effects provide orthogonal contrast to m/z; opens pathway for isomer-resolved MSI in complex biological systems.

model_io.model: Orbitrap secondary ion mass spectrometry (OrbiSIMS) with ion transmission

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structure-dependent secondary-ion dissociation during transmission provides isomer discrimination complementary to m/z separation
hypotheses.result: Isomeric trisaccharides resolved on surfaces; trends align with ion mobility spectrometry

title: Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling
task: Protected bosonic qutrit demonstration via three-photon Kerr parametric oscillator
key_results: Three-photon Rabi oscillations observed; direct Wigner function measurements confirm three-component cat-like states; breathing dynamics reveal energy gap between qutrit and excited states
comments: First experimental demonstration of three-photon KPO as qutrit platform; parasitic pump terms identified as limiting factor for protection.

model_io.model: Three-photon Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cat-qutrit manifold protection manifests as macroscopic temporal interference in phase space
hypotheses.result: Breathing-like dynamics confirmed in mean photon number measurements

title: Tracking the lithiation state of LixSi from machine-learned XPS binding energies
task: Tracking lithiation state of LixSi via machine-learned XPS binding energies and atomistic simulations
key_results: ML-predicted core-level binding energies combined with GCMC/MD sampling capture XPS spectroscopic trends including crystal-to-amorphous disordering during early delithiation; stoichiometry maps correlate local environments to Si 2p signatures
comments: Computational framework bridges ML predictions of XPS with large-scale atomistic sampling; addresses difficulty of characterizing strongly disordered LixSi phases during electrochemical cycling.

model_io.model: Machine-learned XPS binding energies with grand-canonical Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics

hypotheses.hypothesis: ML-predicted binding energies combined with GCMC/MD sampling reveal microstructural evolution during (de)lithiation
hypotheses.result: Stoichiometry maps capture operando/ex situ XPS trends including crystal-amorphous transformation signatures

title: Synthesizability, hardness, and stacking order in multicomponent transition metal carbides from machine-learned potentials
task: Synthesizability and hardness prediction for multicomponent transition metal carbides via machine-learned potentials
key_results: Fine-tuned MACE potential achieves ~10 meV/atom formation energy error; predicted synthesizability at 1500°C agrees with experiments; identified new stacking-ordered phases with formation energies below disordered/hexagonal structures in group 4/5–group 6 metal mixtures
comments: Short-range order contributes only ~few meV/atom; random solid solution approximation valid at high temperature; systematic screening over 1500 equiatomic compositions reveals materials inaccessible in binary systems.

model_io.model: Fine-tuned MACE machine-learned potential trained on ~28,000 DFT calculations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Short-range ordering effects are negligible in multicomponent carbides at high temperature; random solution treatment is valid
hypotheses.result: Stacking-ordered phases with energies below disordered structures emerge in group 4/5–6 mixtures

title: Numerical simulation and structural optimization of electrostatic precipitators for particle purification in space capsules
task: Structural optimization of electrostatic precipitators for aerospace particle purification
key_results: W1-type and single-electrode configurations achieved >92% collection efficiency for 0.2–1.0 μm particles; ~40 percentage-point improvement over flat-plate design for 0.5 μm particles
comments: Coupled DPM-UDS model systematically compares configurations; filter screen adds mechanical stage but increases flow resistance.

model_io.model: Coupled discrete phase model (DPM) with user-defined scalar (UDS) transport

hypotheses.hypothesis: W1-type configuration with corrugated collection plate and auxiliary electrode improves efficiency
hypotheses.result: >92% collection efficiency for 0.2–1.0 μm particles

title: Radionuclide identification for plastic scintillation detectors by backward cumulative channel sum
task: Radionuclide identification in plastic scintillation detectors via backward cumulative channel sum
key_results: BCCS-NNLS method correctly ranked actual radionuclides first for all single-source and binary mixture spectra; residuals 0.48–1.31%; stable rankings under Poisson resampling
comments: Simple linear approach without hardware modification or ML training; limited to fixed libraries and does not address open-set identification or activity quantification.

model_io.model: Plastic scintillation detector with BCCS-NNLS decomposition

hypotheses.hypothesis: BCCS representation combined with NNLS improves interpretability vs. raw-spectrum methods for Compton-dominated spectra
hypotheses.result: Correct ranking of constituents in 18 mixed and single-source test cases; method-specific residuals 0.48–1.31%

title: Controlled nucleation of hopfions with field pulses
task: Deterministic nucleation of magnetic hopfions via field pulses in chiral nanopillars
key_results: Field pulses trigger non-equilibrium dynamics stabilizing isolated hopfions or coexisting 3D solitons depending on pulse amplitude; deterministic nucleation demonstrated without spin-polarized currents
comments: Novel mechanism exploits engineered surface anisotropy to control 3D topological textures; broadens toolkit for nanomagnetism without current-based injection.

model_io.model: Chiral magnetic cylinder with engineered surface uniaxial anisotropy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Field pulse amplitude determines relaxation into distinct topological minima
hypotheses.result: Isolated hopfions or coexisting states with 3D solitons stabilized depending on pulse strength

title: Molecule-aware machine learning for predicting absorption and emission of benzothiadiazole derivatives
task: Structure-aware machine learning for predicting absorption and emission of benzothiadiazole derivatives
key_results: Molecule-aware split reveals random-split R² overestimated by ~27–29 percentage points; count-based Morgan fingerprints reach R²=0.941 (absorption) and 0.916 (emission); deep NN best performance R²=0.954 (absorption) but lacks structure-level extrapolation
comments: Count fingerprints encode donor substructure recurrence, capturing charge-transfer character; emission shows stronger solvent-polarity dependence than absorption; models suited for solvent selection but require structural diversity for new dyes.

model_io.model: Supervised regression with count-based Morgan fingerprints and deep neural networks

hypotheses.hypothesis: Count-based fingerprints better capture charge-transfer character than binary encodings via donor substructure frequency
hypotheses.result: R² improvement from 0.747→0.941 (absorption) and 0.797→0.916 (emission); tertiary amine identified as dominant structural driver

title: Directional magnetic field detection with zero-bias surface acoustic wave sensors
task: Directional magnetic field detection with internally biased surface acoustic wave sensors
key_results: Best sensor detection limit 69 pT/Hz^{1/2} at 10 Hz and 22 pT/Hz^{1/2} at 100 Hz without external bias field; lowest reported for SAW sensors without bias; sinusoidal directional response fits analytical magnetic model
comments: Exchange-biased multilayer structures achieve stable single-domain configuration with low magnetic noise; tilted anisotropy provides internal bias; eliminates external field requirement for portability.

model_io.model: Surface acoustic wave sensor with exchange-biased Ta | (Fe90Co10)78Si12B10 | Ni81Fe19 | Mn80Ir20 | Ta multilayer

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tilted magnetic anisotropy and exchange-bias multilayer structure enable low-noise internal magnetic bias without external field
hypotheses.result: Detection limit 69 pT/Hz^{1/2} at 10 Hz (lowest for zero-bias SAW sensors); sinusoidal directional response fits model
